kill_argument: describe-sample adds no evidence; it relabels it. Its 18 numbers were already computed by prepare-data before the design gate, and the script recomputes them with a near-verbatim copy of prepare_data.py's definitions and then asserts equality to 1e-9, so its only internal check is that two copies of the same code agree. The run exists to turn data-prep metrics into 'analysis' metrics, because result claims must cite analysis runs (the PI's first brief, 033408Z, tried to cite prepare-data directly and the tool refused). It is added after the results gate, so the t1-* claims it will support were never in a results review. I attacked the code and it held: the input hash is checked against data/manifest.json; the definitions (age in 1966 = age76 - 10 with the four bins, regions 1-2/3-4/5-7/8-9, reg76r, smsa66r, parental education over nomomed/nodaded = 0, KWW over non-missing) are those of prepare_data.py; missing values are '' in the CSV and are skipped; flags compare string '1' against prepare's num()==1 and the equality assertion would catch any coding difference; nothing relates nearc4 to schooling or wages; failures exit before metrics are written. The substantive check is the 0.05 rule against Card's printed values, which gives 15/18.

findings.text: D7 adds result claims (t1-*) after the results gate and after results-r2, so no results review covers them, and the paper currently says the opposite of what will be true: the summary-statistics paragraph says the Table 1 comparison 'is a data check and enters no result claim'. Two of the three misses are one man from the rounding boundary (age 18-20: 742 men = 24.651%, 741 would round to 24.6; South 1976: 1,215 = 40.365%, 1,214 would give 40.332), and data/CODEBOOK.md reads the black-share miss as 'a transcription error in Table 1', which is a guess. Remedy (no code change): the paper states that D7 was added at the paper stage after the results gate and that describe-sample recomputes the prepare-data values; the 'enters no result claim' sentence is rewritten; the black-share miss is reported as unexplained (or as a guess, labelled as such); paper-r1 checks each t1-* claim against runs/describe-sample/metrics.json.
findings.evidence: plan.json design.deviations D7 and task dr-describe; paper/main.tex summary-statistics paragraph ('the comparison is a data check and enters no result claim'); data/CODEBOOK.md 'Discrepancies, stated plainly'; data/prepare_metrics.json t1_sample_age66_18_20_pct 24.6512, t1_sample_south76_pct 40.3654, t1_sample_black_pct 23.3555
